cases.narrative: At 10:30 p.m. on January 19, 2015, Employee #1, a supervisor employed aconstruction company, was supervising a crew of workers engaged in thedemolition of a bridge overpass. The bridge, which was a double-hingedsuspension type, passed over an interstate highway. The workers weredemolishing the bridge from east to west. The tie-down system that had beeninstalled earlier that day failed, and the center span of the bridge collapsedto the highway below. Employee #1, who was on the bridge when the center spancollapsed, was struck and pinned underneath the tracks of a Komatsu PC400excavator. He sustained crushing injuries to the head and was killed.

At 3:30 p.m. on January 30, 2015, Employee #1 and Coworkers #1, #2, #3, and #4,all employed by a steel construction company, and Coworker #5, employed by adifferent contractor, were working at a 26-story multifamily residentialbuilding project. Coworker #5, a crane technician, was directing the craneassembly and disassembly operations. Employee #1 and Coworkers #1 through #4had completed the erection of a tower crane and were lowering the climbing unit. They were monitoring the unit’s descent when Employee #1 became caught betweenthe climbing unit and the frame of the tower crane. Emergency services werecalled, and Employee #1 was transported to the hospital. Upon arrival, he waspronounced dead. The report indicated there were no witnesses to this fatalevent. Employee #1 died as a result of crushing injuries to multiple parts ofhis body.
At 3:45 p.m. on May 4, 2015, an employee was installing drainage pipes when thetrench collapsed. The employee was buried and died from asphyxiation.

At approximately 2:00 p.m. on June 5, 2015, Employee #1 was installing andhooking up new hydraulic lines and fittings on a portable grout-mud mixer. Thedrum of the grout-mud mixer was raised and Employee #1 was sitting under thedrum. A hydraulic fitting either came loose or was removed and the drum camedown trapping and crushing him. He was bent at the waist with the drum sittingon his back and died.

At 9:00 a.m. on July 8, 2015, an employee was guiding a gasoline tamper from aCase brand 580 Super L loader backhoe bucket as it was lowered into anexcavation. The backhoe fell into the excavation as the backhoe bucket waslowered and fell on top of the employee; crushing the employee.

At 6:30 a.m. on October 1, 2015, an employee was positioning an aerial lift toremove existing gutters from structure. While operating the aerial lift, theemployee was killed due to asphyxiation when he was crushed between the liftbasket and the roof soffit.

At 1:37 p.m., on June 15, 2016, three employees were installing a 4 inch sewerline in a 12 ft. trench. The employee a 33 year old male, was inside the trenchleveling out the bottom when the walls of the trench collapsed, trapping andkilling the employee underneath.

At 4:20 p.m. on March 9, 2017, an employee was installing SITEDRAIN Strip 6000Series on the interior side of a trench. The SITEDRAI Strip 6000 Series becamefolded and employees were unable to pour gravel onto it. The employee enteredthe trench, approximately 40 feet from strip needing to be corrected, from thebackfilled side and ran to go adjust the strip. The employee adjusted the stripto its desired position when the trench caved in, covering his entire bodyunderneath. The employee was killed.

At approximately 4:00 p.m. on March 23, 2017, Employee #1, a carpenter, was drilling 0.25-inch holes in a precast concrete ceiling panel working from a 10 foot high step ladder. He was found on the floor with the ladder on top of him, dead.

At 10:25 a.m. on May 17, 2017, an employee was driving a scissor lift through a8 foot tall door opening and had to cross over a plywood board that covered a 20inch wide by 6 inch deep drainage ditch. As the employee was crossing theplywood, it snapped and the scissor lift got stuck a ditch that the board wascovering. A coworker used another scissor lift to pull the employee and hisscissor lift from the ditch. The stuck scissor lift was freed unexpectedly, resulting in the employee’s head being crushed between a 6 inch thick concretewall and the rail of the scissor lift. The employee was killed.

At 1:45 p.m. on June 6, 2017, an employee was pulling low voltage wire when hebecame crushed between the basket of an aerial lift and a red iron bar of aceiling. The employee suffered a broken vertebrae at the C3 location and waskilled.

At 9:00 a.m. on November 7, 2017, an employee was assisting in the installationof an 8 inch by 14 foot piece of PVC sewer pipe into an 8 foot trench. Thenorth wall of the trench closest to the excavator sheered into the trenchengulfing the employee. The employee was killed.

At 10:30 a.m. on March 8, 2018, Employee #1 was shimming a piece of 2 inch by 4 inch lumber underneath a rack stand while a coworker was hitting a stand, loaded by a rebar cage, with a sledgehammer. The rebar cage shifted, causing the rack stand to fall over and trap Employee #1 between the rebar cage and the horizontal beam of the rack stand. Employee #1’s torso was crushed, resulting in his death.

At 2:00 p.m. on March 22, 2018, Employee #1 was assisting in the placement of alarge steel awning above the front entry way of a house. While suspended, thesteel canopy became dislodged and suddenly moved towards the exterior wall ofthe house. Employee #1’s head became caught between the house and the steelporch canopy. Employee #1 suffered a crushing traumatic head injury and waskilled.

At 3:30 p.m. on May 2, 2018, an employee was cutting the last section ofironwork that was holding a catwalk which was suspended by a crane during somedemolition work. The catwalk became snagged and the employee signaled the craneoperator to raise the load slightly. The load was freed but started to tilt andshift. The employee made an attempt to get back onto the catwalk but was struckand pinned against the guardrail. The employee suffered six broken rails, several broken bones on his spine, and lacerations to his liver and kidney. Theemployee died from the injuries several days later.

At 9:45 a.m. on September 13, 2018, an employee was assisting in the dismantlingof a barn. As the employee was using a chainsaw to cut the overhead section ofthe barn floor, a forklift was lifting a precut section. During work, theoverhead floor collapsed and trapped the employee and coworkers beneath thedebris. The employee suffered a broken neck and was killed. However, the othercoworkers survived with only one sustaining a laceration to the back of hishead.

On December 18, 2018, an employee was taking depth measurements with anengineering rod. The trench collapsed below the worker standing at the 11-footedge. The employee was crushed and killed due to asphyxiation.

At 3:30 p.m. on April 9, 2019, an employee was using a Stihl gas poweredcircular saw to cut the bell off a section of 18" concrete pipe. The employeewas struck in the neck when the saw kicked back and hit him, lacerating hisneck. The employee was killed.

At 3:00 p.m. on July 23, 2019, Employees #1 and #2, employed by a drainage services company, were working in a trench at the site of a residential structure. The trench sidewall collapsed, and the two employees were buried under approximately 2 feet of soil. Employees #1 and #2 were killed, cause of death asphyxiation.

At 1:30 p.m. on November 25, 2019, an employee spraying water onto concretecolumns underneath the framework constructed to hold a concrete pour of theseventh floor of a building under construction. The poured concrete weighed morethan the form could accommodate and the seventh floor collapsed onto theemployee. The employee was killed by crushing injuries sustained when theconcrete fell on him.

At 5:00 p.m. on January 20, 2020, Employee #1, employed by a pipelinecontractor, was engaged in maintenance work, looking for the source of a fluidleaking from a front end loader. The loader was parked with its bucket restingon a raised mat/dock. The employee loosened the first hydraulic hose to accessthe second hose, which was leaking. As he started to loosen the second hose, the bucket fell/descended, and he was pinned between the loader arm that washolding the bucket and the loader frame. Employee #1 sustained crushinginjuries and was killed.
At 9:50 a.m. on February 17, 2020, an employee was working in an eight foot deeptrench laying drainage pipe. While working a side-wall cave-in occurred thatburied the employee and killed him.

At 1:00 p.m. on December 18, 2020, Employee #1 and a coworker, employed by aconstruction company, were engaged in site preparation for a planned multifamilyresidential structure. The coworker was operating an excavator and digging atrench where a sewer pipe was being removed. Employee #1 was spotting for hiscoworker. For no apparent reason, Employee #1 entered the trench, which was notprotected from collapse. His coworker subsequently stated that he told Employee#1 to get out of the trench. As Employee #1 moved toward a ladder to exit thetrench, a trench wall collapsed. Employee #1 was buried in approximately 8 feetof dirt. It took approximately 20 minutes for his coworker and others toextricate Employee #1 from the trench. CPR was performed unsuccessfully. Employee #1 was killed by asphyxia.
At 1:00 p.m. on February 5, 2021, an employee entered an excavation to check fora water leak in a sewer line. At some point, the wall of the excavationcollapsed, buried in soil, killed the employee.

At 12:00 p.m. on April 7, 2021, an employee inspected the "rock rake" attachmenton a skid steer to remove debris. At some point, the employee’s head/neck becamecaught in the attachment, received a neck fracture, and was killed.

At 11:27 a.m. on August 5, 2021, an employee worked in an excavation to packdown soil while a coworker operated an excavator at the edge of the excavation. At some point, the soil under the excavator collapsed and the excavator fellinto the excavation onto the employee. The employee received crushing injuriesto the abdomen and pelvis and was killed.
At 12:36 p.m. on May 4, 2021, an employee worked to expose a pipe on thesidewall of the trench. At some point, the trench collapsed onto the employee, who was asphyxiated and killed.

At 10:45 a.m. on December 27, 2021, an employee installed sprinkler heads for anew overhead sprinkler system. At some point, the employee became caught betweenthe railing of the lift and a steel girder, asphyxiated, and was killed.

At 10:15 a.m. on October 5, 2022, an employee was scooping dirt away from anexcavation with a TEREX 600 Auger Bit. The employee was using the auger bit todrill a pier hole. He fell into the pier hole and was crushed by the auger bit. The employee died from massive head and body trauma.

At 3:30 p.m. on August 27, 2024, an employee working as a construction laborerfor a water and sewer line contractor was working in a 27-foot-long by14-foot-deep trench. Several feet of the trench were not protected by a trenchbox or sloping. The trench collapsed on the employee crushing him. The employeedied from asphyxiation.
At 5:00 p.m. on May 16, 2015, an employee was operating an aerial lift, contacted overhead power lines, and was electrocuted to death.
At 3:21 p.m. on May 13, 2015, an employee was walking across a roof whenlightning struck a direct hit. The employee suffered fatal burns to head andwas electrocuted.

At approximately 2:15 p.m. on June 19, 2015, Employee #1 was pulling wire fromHVAC coolers into an energized 480 volt switch gear room. He came in contactwith an exposed 480 volt transformer and was electrocuted.

At 10:15 p.m. on January 21, 2105, an employee was carrying a piece of aluminumflashing up a ladder. The victim lost control of the flashing in the windyconditions. The flashing contacted the adjacent energized power line. Thevictim was electrically shocked which caused him to fall approximately 18 feetfrom the ladder. Employee succumbed to injuries and died.

At approximately 12:45 p.m. on September 1, 2015, an employee was working froman aluminum extension ladder removing satellite dishes from the exterior of atwo story multi-unit residential building. The employee had positioned theladder so that it was resting on the energized electrical power service to thebuilding. During the course of the work the employee was shocked and fell fromthe ladder, approximately 1.5 stories up, striking his head on the asphaltdriveway and was killed.

At approximately 9:39 a.m. on September 9, 2015, an employee was aligning a new750 volt transformer on a concrete pad. The employee was leaning against anexisting 480 volt 3 phase metal cabinet using it as leverage to push the newtransformer into place. While pushing on the outside of the existing metalcabinet, the employee reduced the distance between the cabinet and the bus barcausing an arc flash. The employee received burns to 60% of his upper body andwas killed.
At 10:30 a.m. on July 9, 2015, an employee was changing a light bulb in aswimming pool. The employee was electrocuted when they contacted a live circuitthat was supposed to be off.

At 11:24 a.m. on May 5, 2016, The owner and employee were standing at oppositesides of an asphalt paver waiting for a dump truck to unload asphalt into thepaver. The owner was operating the paver and the employee was on the oppositeside of the paver, observing and making sure the paver stayed full. The paveroperator motioned for the dump truck driver to unload the asphalt into thepaver. When the bed of the dump truck was raised, it made contact with anoverhead power line (7,200 volt phase to ground) that was located approximately16 feet, 4 inches above ground level. The employee was electrocuted and killed.electrocuted and killed.

At 12:30 p.m., on June 9, 2016, an employee was epreparing a worksite forinstallation of a new utility pole. A boom truck contacted an energized 13800volt transmission line. The employee sustained contact from the chest area tothe right arm, was electrocuted and killed.
At 8:15 a.m. on April 7, 2016, an employee was killed from an electrical burn.
At approximately 12:00 a.m. on July 24, 2016, Employee #1 was servicing a coiland condenser in a residential attic. He was found unconscious and died fromelectrocution.

At 10:48 p.m. on November 22, 2016, an employee was installing rain gutters. The ladder the employee was using came into contact with electrical power lines, and the employees was electrocuted and died.
At approximately 6:30 p.m. on March 16, 2017, Employee #1 was electrocuted.

At 11:00 a.m. on June 23, 2017, an employee was working from a ladder to installa part in an air conditioning system. While he was working with wiring, hesuffered an electric shock. The employee fell from the ladder and struck hishead. The employee died as a result of his head injury.

At 4:30 p.m. on October 9, 2017, Employee #1 was using a dump truck to fill atrench with Dirt. After dropping a load, with the bed of the truck still raised, Employee #1 began driving forward. However, the raised truck bed was too talland came in contact with an overhead power line. Contact with the live wireresulted in Employee #1 being electrocuted.

At 9:15 a.m. on November 29, 2017, Employee #1 was operating the controls of thedrill tower belonging to a drill mounted drill rig. The drill tower made contactwith an energized overhead power line. Employee #1 was electrocuted and killed.
At 8:30 a.m. on May 23, 2018, an employee was installing a flexible all-weatherelectrical conduit when he was electrocuted.
At 8:25 a.m. on October 5, 2018, an employee was installing a ground line for awork table and touched a live circuit, electrocuting himself.

At 5:10 p.m. on March 28, 2019, an employee was working on a crew that wastasked with pouring a cement foundation for high mast light poles. The employeewas standing/sitting on the rear of a boom truck as the boom truck operatorremoved a 41.83 foot tremie pipe used to pour the cement. As the pipe was laidon the ground, the boom contacted a 7,620 Volt overhead power line. The boomtruck was energized and the employee was electrocuted.

At 11:30 a.m. on June 1, 2019, Employee #1, employed by a construction company, was engaged in demolition work at a one-story building that was being renovated. He was attempting to remove drywall from around piping and other installedmechanical equipment. A nearby junction box had been left open by otheremployees working earlier in this space. Employee #1 came into contact withlive wires extending from the box, and he was exposed to 227 volts ofelectricity. Employee #1 was electrocuted.

At 12:30 p.m. on August 9, 2019, Employee #1, employed by a construction andelectrical services company, was installing a new LED light fixture on top of a25-foot tank. The lighting circuit was energized to 110/120 volts. Employee #1sustained an electric shock, fell from the tank, and struck his head against anadjacent steel tank. He was wearing fall protection. Employee #1 was killed. Employee #1 was killed.

At 11:00 a.m. on October 11, 2019, Employee #1 was performing interior plumbing, and conducting electrical and duct work installation, in a commercialconstruction project. While connecting the emergency lighting fixture to anemergency circuit junction box, Employee #1 came into contact with a live andenergized circuit, was electrocuted, and then killed.

At 8:00 a.m. on October 11, 2019, Employee #1, Employee #2, and Employee #3, allworking as carpenters for a siding contractor, were erecting a pump jackscaffold support pole. The employees had the support pole raised into the airwhen the wind blew the support pole into a 26-killivolt power line. All threeemployees were shocked as a result. Employee #1 received burns to his arms, backand torso and died as a result of his injuries. Employee #2 received burns tohis hands and was hospitalized. Employee #3 received burns to his back and washospitalized.

At 12:30 p.m. on January 17, 2020, Employee #1, employed by a gutters company, was working at a multiemployer construction project, a two-story multifamilyresidential structure. He was working from a ladder and attempting to hoist a53-foot section of aluminum gutter for installation. The gutter came intocontact with a 13 kilovolt electrical power line. A surge of electrical powertravelled through the gutter to Employee #1, who was electrocuted.
At 2:00 p.m. on April 20, 2020, Employee #1, employed by a construction company, was engaged in a power line installation. The employee was electrocuted.electrocuted.

At 1:55 p.m. on March 2, 2021, an employee worked in an excavation to spliceexisting streetlight wires. At some point, the tool used for the splice madecontact with a live 480-volt wire. The employee was killed by electrocution.
At 2:30 p.m. on June 8, 2021, an employee climbed a utility pole and madecontact with a live overhead power line. The employee was electrocuted, receivedsevere burns to the body and was killed.
At 3:30 p.m. on July 29, 2021, an employee worked to disconnect power from anoverhead (23 KV) powerline. At some point, the employee contacted the live powerline, was electrocuted, and killed.
At 2:00 p.m. on July 24, 2023, an employee working as a roofer for a roofingcontractor was sitting under a tree. The employee was struck by lightning andkilled due to electrocution.

At 1:10 p.m. on August 15, 2023, an employee was welding piping in a paperproduction facility when he was found unresponsive. It was determined that theemployee contacted a live electrical component and was electrocuted.

At 12:00 a.m. on January 14, 2016, an employee was installing ceiling joists onthe second floor of a residential single family dwelling construction site. Theemployee was in process of coming down from the top plate when he lost hisbalance and fell from the top plate of the second floor. The employee struck hishead on the frozen ground below which also had rocks. Fall distance wasestimated to be over 24 feet. Employee sustained a traumatic brain injury, compromised airway, multiple head and neck wounds, and was unresponsive whenmedical attention arrived. Employee died four days later as a result of hisinjuries.
On January 13, 2016, an employee was standing on a ladder. The employee fellfrom the ladder to the floor and was killed as a result of head injuries.

At approximately 4:30 a.m. on January 18, 2017, an employee was climbing theframes and cross bracing of a tubular welded frame scaffold in order to reach anelevated work platform. He fell 40 feet from the scaffold to a concrete slabbelow. The employee suffered severe trauma, including suspected multiplefractures, to all parts of the worker’s body upon impact with the concrete slaband was killed.
At 2:30 p.m. on June 13, 2017, an employee fell from a scaffold while painting. He suffered a concussion and died as a result.
At 9:15 a.m. on March 23, 2018, an employee was installing metal decking on theroof of a commercial building when he fell 22 feet from the roof and was killed.
At 12:15 p.m. on June 11, 2018, an employee was walking on the top of a buss duct or other electrical equipment. The employee fell 14 feet to the floor, sustained a head injury, and died.
At 8:30 a.m. on January 15, 2019, an employee was installing a residential roofand fell approximately 21 feet to the ground. The employee was killed fromsevere head trauma.
At 5:32 p.m. on January 31, 2019, an employee was climbing a ladder and fell, fracturing her arm when she landed on the floor.

At 4:00 p.m. on January 29, 2019, an employee was installing 1.5-inch gas lineson the second floor of a newly built residential house when he lost his balanceand fell backwards into a 2x4 stud. The employee rolled approximately 8 feetdown the staircase before stopping. The employee was killed from blunt forcetrauma to his head and neck.
At 9:45 a.m. on November 19, 2018, an employee was throwing shingles off theedge of a house. The employee lost his footing and fell from the roof to theconcrete driveway below and was killed.

At 11:00 a.m. on April 23, 2019, an employee was using a 10 foot tall A-frameladder to unfasten bolts in order to remove the face of a metal sign. Theemployee lost balance, fell to the pavement, and was killed due to a skullfracture.

At 3:30 p.m. on July 29, 2019, the owner of a construction company, was paintingthe exterior of a commercial building. He was working from a plank placed onthe corner of the roof and a fabricated frame scaffold when he fell from theplank, a fall height of 14 feet, and was killed.

At 7:30 a.m. on July 31, 2019, Employee #1, employed by a home builder, was working at the site of a new two-story residential structure. He was installing .75 inch plywood decking to second-story structural beams. Employee #1 fell, a fall height of approximately 20 feet, and struck the basement’s concrete floor. Emergency services transported Employee #1 to the hospital, where he died from injuries sustained in the fall.

At 3:45 p.m. on July 18, 2019, Employee #1, employed by a concrete company, was working at the site of a new two-story multifamily residential building. He was standing on a 6-foot ladder when he fell. Employee #1 sustained fatal head and chest injuries.

At 8:30 a.m. on August 28, 2019, Employee #1 was working at a multiemployerconstruction project, a three-story multifamily residential building. He wasworking from a ladder and installing siding on the chimney. Employee #1 fell, afall height of 30 feet. Employee #1 was killed.

At 11:45 a.m. on December 15, 2019, Employee #1 and a coworker, employed by aroofing company, were engaged in reroofing work at a one-story commercialbuilding. They were installing a membrane of thermoplastic polyolefin (TPO)over the existing metal roof. The coworker removed a roof ridge, which createdan unprotected 14-inch gap in the roof’s surface. Employee #1 walked by the gapand fell through it to the concrete floor, a fall height of 30 feet. Employee#1 sustained traumatic blunt force injuries and was killed.

At 1:30 p.m. on January 20, 2020, Employee #1, employed by a constructioncompany, was working at a one story residential structure and installingshingles on the roof of a new garage. The employee fell and struck his head onthe ground. He sustained traumatic head injury and was killed.

At 7:50 a.m. on November 18, 2020, Employee #1, employed by a roofing company, was engaged in roofing work at a residential structure. He was sitting at theroof’s peak with bundles of shingles when he fell, a fall height of 22 feet, andstruck the concrete surface. Employee #1 sustained multiple blunt force traumainjuries and was killed.

At 11:30 a.m. on March 6, 2021, an employee replaced a board on a porch roof andthen began the process to shingle the roof. At some point, the employee steppedon the newly installed board, which became loose, lost balance, fellapproximately twelve feet, and was killed by head, neck and spine trauma.

At 7:30 p.m. on April 26, 2021, an employee performed framing work when theyslipped off the elevated work surface and fell approximately nine feet. Theemployee was killed by blunt force trauma to the head.
At 9:30 a.m. on November 2, 2021, an employee worked to paint an exterior walland fell approximately ten feet. The employee was killed by trauma to the body.

At 10:30 a.m. on March 23, 2022, an employee was looking for the cause of a roofleak. The employee walked in an area where there was a skylight and fell throughit to the concrete floor. The employee was killed due to blunt force trauma tothe head and body.

At 1:00 p.m. on October 17, 2022, an employee was working, sweeping and cleaningaround uncovered, five foot deep, excavated holes, that were 18 inches wide whenhe dropped his phone into one of the holes. The holes where partially filledwith water due to rain that occurred the previous evening. The employee bentinto the hole to retrieve it and fell in head first. The employee was unable toget himself out of the hole and drowned.

At 12:00 p.m. on March 27, 2023, an employee was applying sealant to the roof ofa structure. The employee fell to the ground. The employee was killed andsuffered the following injuries: left shoulder deformity; bleeding from nose, mouth, and ear; laceration above ear; and collapsed lung.
At 11:00 a.m. on May 18, 2023, an employee was in an unprotected 10 foot trench, leveling gravel underneath a 24-inch PVC sewer line. The employee was killed.

At 2:00 p.m. on June 1, 2023, an employee was connecting electrical service fromthe street to the second floor of the house. The employee fell from the scaffoldto the driveway while connecting electrical service to the house. The employeefell on his head and was taken to the hospital, where he was pronounced dead.

At 11:24 a.m. on May 27, 2023, an employee was descending a ladder and slipped. The employee lost his balance and fell striking a propane grill and the ground. The employee sustained head trauma and died three days later.

At 12:30 pm, on October 3, 2023, Employee #1 was working for a constructionroofing contractor. Employee #1 was removing shingles on a steep slope roof, and he fell approximately 24 feet from the edge of the roof. Blunt force traumafrom the fall led to the fatality of Employee #1.

At 4:00 p.m. on August 12, 2024, Employee #1 was leaving the roof to return tothe floor at the end of the workday when he fell from a scissor lift to theconcrete. The employee sustained multiple injuries from the fall. Emergencyresponders were called to the scene, but the employee was pronounced dead fromthe injuries sustained upon impact with the concrete floor.

At 6:00 p.m. on August 7, 2024, an employee was descending a ladder at a newhome construction site when he fell backward to the ground. A nearby homeownerwitnessed the incident and provided CPR until emergency services arrived. Theemployee was transported to the hospital, where he later died from his injuries.

At 6:44 p.m. on January 29, 2015, two employees were carrying a piece of achicken rack (leg) to a staging area. The legs were being set on their edge andleaned against the inside of an exterior wall of the building that the employeeswere working in. The employees set the leg down on the ground against a stackof legs that had already been set down and stacked. As the employees set theleg onto the existing stack, the stack began to fall away from the wall. Theemployee began to back out of the way of the falling stack of legs. As theemployee was backing out of the way, he tripped and fell to the floor, strikinghis head on the platform of an aerial lift that was parked nearby. The employeeshead struck the steel platform of an aerial lift where he suffered a major headinjury and died.
At 11:00 a.m. on May 4, 2015, an employee carried metal studs into worksite. Theemployee tripped or collapsed and struck head against a rock wall. The employeewas found non-responsive and later died.

At 7:30 p.m. on February 25, 2016, an employee who just arrived at the worksitewas exiting a truck, slipped on ice, and struck his head on the asphalt parkinglot. Following the incident, the employee told co-workers about the incidentand said did not feel well. The employee was admitted to the hospital, developed a coma, and died March 15, 2016, from blunt force trauma to the head.trauma to the head.

At 5:00 p.m. on September 7, 2016, an employee was taking a break, walking to orfrom the bathroom. The employee fainted and fell backwards, he hit his head onthe floor and was killed from a head laceration.

At 11:00 a.m. on October 5, 2016, an employee was planning some conduit routingwhen he tripped over an unprotected edge and fell to the floor, striking hishead as he fell. The employee had a head injury and multiple body injuries.body injuries.

On April 3, 2017, an employee fell to the ground while walking. He was impaledby a screwdriver resulting in puncture of aorta. The employee was taken to thePresbyterian hospital where he died the following day.

At 10:00 a.m. on February 8, 2018, an employee had loaded a furnace in the backof a truck before falling backwards and striking his head onto the concretesurface. The employee was killed as a result of his injuries.

At 2:00 p.m. on March 7, 2018, per the employee’s wife, the employee wasretrieving tools/equipment from a work van when he lost his footing and fellbackwards. He hit his head; however, did not report the incident. When he washospitalized an approximate month later for a hematoma to his head, the employeedied.

At 3:00 p.m. on August 21, 2018, an employee was using guide lines while afiberglass pool was being unloaded from a delivery trailer. The employee jumpedonto the trailer and started to push against the pools to speed up the unloadingand lost his balance, falling against the jagged edge of the top pool. Theemployee cut his face and lacerated the main arteries in his neck, killing him.killing him.

At 12:00 p.m. on June 25, 2020, Employee #1, employed by a construction company, was engaged in form work for a new road. He was using a sledge hammer to set aform stake for a footing. The employee missed the stake, and the weight of thehammer caused the employee to twist and fall on his right knee. The employeewas transported to the hospital and treated for a sprained right knee and a tornmedial meniscus. The employee required amputation above the right knee. Aninfection developed, and Employee #1 died from complications of the originalinjury.

At 8:30 a.m. on January 28, 2020, an employee parked a trailer. While walking ona skid steer, the employee tripped, fell, and received a liver laceration. Theemployee was hospitalized to treat the injury, but later died.

At 11:00 a.m. on November 18, 2021, an employee transported a load of scrap in apersonal trailer to be disposed of. While attempting to open the trailer door, the employee lost balance and fell backward receiving a contusion to the lowerback and hip area. The employee then later went to the hospital for treatmentfor pain. The employee then went home and later that night died for unknownreasons.

At 2:30 p.m. on June 9, 2022,, an employee was using a manual cutter to cut a 10foot, 3.5 inch diameter metal pipe when he stood up from a crouching position, stumbled, and slid to the floor. The employee was pronounced dead on the sceneby emergency services.
