An employee was doing decking work at a new construction site. The employee fell more than 6 feet to the ground and suffered a broken hand/wrist and a broken hip.

A concrete panel was standing upright on the ground, rigged for lifting and secured from falling over. An employee was on a ladder, unhooking crane rigging, when the crane boom was lowered. The panel leaned toward him and he jumped off the ladder, thinking it was about to fall over. He landed on both feet and suffered fractures to both heels. He was hospitalized.

An employee was on a 10-foot step ladder that was leaning against a wall. The employee was hanging a poly barrier when the ladder slipped, causing them to fall to the concrete below and suffer broken ribs.
An employee was removing metal roof panels. The employee fell through the roof to the ground about 15 feet below, suffered a broken elbow, and was hospitalized.

An employee was working on an extension ladder inside of a residence when the ladder slipped out from underneath him. The employee fell approximately 8-9 feet onto the tile floor and sustained a femur fracture.

An employee was descending an aluminum extension ladder with tools when he tripped and fell approximately eight feet to the ground, landing on rocks and a garden bed. He fractured two ribs and one vertebra.

An employee was descending the ladder of a tube and coupler scaffold system when they missed a rung and fell four to six feet to the concrete ground. The employee sustained injuries to their left hip, wrist and forehead.

An employee was scraping the roof of an auditorium at a middle school. They were standing on a two-tier portable scaffold on wheels. The scaffold moved and the employee fell approximately 15 feet to the ground below, resulting in head trauma.

An employee was moving material on a roof. The employee fell 14 feet from the roof to the top floor of the building beneath, striking the concrete floor. He sustained a partial thickness injury to the back of his head requiring staples, fractured left ribs, and a spinal injury requiring surgery.

On May 15, 2025, two employees were laying out waterproofing membrane material on the balcony of a new residence. The injured employee was unrolling the membrane when he stepped off the edge of the roof adjacent to the balcony. The employee fell approximately 13.5 feet to the ground and sustained a fractured pelvic bone.

An employee was removing an existing flat roof and throwing debris into the trash dumpster from the edge of the roof. The employee slipped and fell approximately 15 feet into the dumpster, landing on debris. The employee was hospitalized with a laceration to the head and two fractured vertebrae.

An employee was standing on a scaffold plank, performing masonry work and chipping concrete at a wall corner. The employee fell from the plank and landed on the ground, suffering a closed fracture to the left ankle.
An employee was hospitalized for a possible concussion, after falling down some stairs.
An employee was cleaning equipment, slipped in the mud, and fractured the right fibula.
An employee tripped and stepped into an open manhole. He fell across the manhole, fracturing two ribs and puncturing a lung.
During excavation work, an employee stepped on loose soil and rolled his right ankle while spotting for the excavator. The employee’s right ankle was dislocated.
An employee was setting windows on the first floor when he lost his balance, fell backward, and struck his head on a concrete parking block.
An employee fell down the stairs and suffered head trauma, requiring hospitalization.
An employee was getting lunch meat from the cooler box and walking back to the slicer when her foot got tangled in a box strap causing her to fall and injure her right hip.
An employee was installing ground rod, slipped, and injured his left palm.
An employee was picking up a roll of rubber in the storage shed and lost his footing. He fell on the 4" storage lip and broke his hip.
An employee slipped and fell to the same level while trying to use the first step on a scaffold access ladder. The employee hit and injured their ribs and was hospitalized.
An employee tossed a dirt clod at the injured employee, who lost his balance, fell to the ground, and fractured his right arm while trying to break his fall.
An employee slipped on ice and hit his leg on the underside of a trailer, fracturing both bones in his leg and requiring hospitalization.
While walking and working on the road widener machine, an employee fell and broke his left ankle.
An employee was taping/finishing drywall when he miss-stepped and fell, breaking his wrist.
An employee slipped and fell while exiting a truck fracturing the tail bone.

An employee removed his shoes upon entering a customer’s home so as not to soil the customer’s floor. As he was taking the stairs leading to the patio, he slipped and fell, hitting his head on the floor and requiring hospitalization for a brain bleed.
An employee was moving waste lumber. The lumber slipped and the employee fell to the floor as he tried to move out of the way. His left wrist was broken.
While walking, an employee slipped on icy ground and fell resulting in fractures to the right fibula and tibia.

An employee had been doing plumbing work at a warehouse. At the end of his shift, he was stepping into his truck when he lost consciousness, fell backwards, and struck his head on the concrete. He was hospitalized.
An employee slipped and fell in an icy parking lot. The employee sustained fractured ribs and a fractured L1 vertebra.
An employee tripped while walking out of a building and fell forward into a door. The employee suffered facial injuries, a dislocated shoulder, and a broken foot.
An employee was spraying a column with fireproofing material. He slipped on the wet floor and fell on his side, suffering a broken hip. He was hospitalized.
An employee was walking out of a construction trailer when she slipped on ice and fell to the ground, resulting in a broken leg. The employee was admitted to the hospital for surgery.

An employee and a co-worker were feeding a cable through framed metal studs. After the task was complete, the employee walked over to his co-worker and his foot became caught on the cable, causing him to lose his balance and fall. The employee sustained a forearm laceration from a framed metal stud.
On January 18, 2024, an employee sustained head and neck injuries after falling down a staircase at a customer’s home.
An employee was helping to get a loader running. The employee slipped on ice and hit his head and right shoulder. He suffered an injury to the shoulder.
An employee was walking across a site to get rebar when he stepped on a wooden stake. The stake broke, causing the employee to sustain fractures to his left ankle/leg and lacerations.

On May 4, 2025, at approximately 12:45 PM, an employee was walking to her car when she fell and a piece of metal mesh penetrated the skin of her forehead. The employee was hospitalized and required surgery.

An employee was walking backward while unspooling wire from a reel when they tripped over the leg of a duct lift dolly and fell to the concrete floor. The employee sustained a lumbar injury and was hospitalized.

An employee was walking under a section of scaffold when he tripped over one of the scaffold bars around the base. He landed on his hip on top of a small piece of metal grating, which had a toeboard installed around a small opening. The employee fractured the femoral head on his right hip and was hospitalized.

Employee was working on the carburetor of his company vehicle with gasoline on his hands when it ignited, causing 2nd and 3rd degree burns on his right hand and 2nd degree burns on his stomach and left hand. Employee was treated and hospitalized at Doctor’s Hospital in Augusta, Georgia.
An employee was heating up sealer on a seal coating sprayer. The employee lifted up the lid of the sealer container and a flame shot out, burning the employee’s left hand and forearm.

An employee was welding pipe as part of a compressor change-out when pressurized oil in the pipe released and ignited. The employee suffered burns to his wrists and face and was hospitalized for treatment.
On August 26, 2016, at approximately 10:30 AM an employee was cutting a barrel. The barrel exploded and the employee suffered several burns and broke his left leg.

An employee was refueling a job site crew boat on 10/31/16. He removed the boat battery to plug in the portable fuel pump. During fueling, some fuel ran over and spilled inside the boat. He turned off the fuel pump, cleaned up the area, and reinstalled the boat battery. A fire occurred. He put the fire out with a fire extinguisher and suffered hand and arm pain.
Two employees were cleaning out a tank with a vacuum hose and an air lamp when a flash fire occurred burning both employees on the face.
An employee was removing a plug from a 6-inch pipeline when pressure in the line caused it to blow off and strike his hand and arm, requiring surgery.

One employee was in the back of a box truck while a second employee was standing outside when an air compressor exploded in the box truck’s engine compartment. One of the employees was hospitalized with burns.
An employee was pouring gas into a gasoline-powered pump when the gas ignited and burned the employee’s chest and legs.
An employee was cleaning the interior of a gasoline storage tank using a power washer to facilitate disposal. A fire in the tank caused third-degree burns to the employee’s face and hands.
An employee’s left ring finger was amputated after a pressurized airline ruptured in his hand.
While an employee was preparing a coupler for installation on a pipeline, residual natural gas flared and caught fire. The employee was hospitalized with burns to the face and arms.

An employee was refilling a blast pot for sand blasting operations. When the lid of the blast pot was loosened, pressure was released and the blasting media was discharged into his face. The force also knocked him back, causing him to fall and strike his head on another blasting pot. The employee was hospitalized with abrasions to the face and eyes and injuries to his head.

Two employees were working on a 16-inch plastic water pipe, drilling for a saddle tap when the pipe exploded. One employee suffered an amputation of the right arm, a laceration to the right leg, and the loss of vision in the right eye. The second employee suffered lacerations to the legs and sand in the eyes.
An employee was troubleshooting an air conditioner. The discharge line exploded, and a piece of the copper line went into the employee’s leg.

An employee was mixing two-cycle fuel for a concrete saw when sparks from concrete sawing ignited the gasoline vapors, causing a fire and burning the employee. The employee sustained severe burns to the hands, neck, and face.

Employees were making emergency repairs to the girder of a bridge that was struck by a tractor-trailer. The injured employee was waiting for grinding to be completed so he could stick-weld. He was standing next to a hanging torch when a spark from the grinding caused leaking propane to ignite. The employee sustained a flash burn to his right ankle and required hospitalization.

A crew was performing temporary asphalt placement when the walk-behind pavement roller they were using ran out of gasoline. The injured employee went to refuel it with gasoline when a fire occurred, causing the employee to sustain burns to the head, neck and chest, and hand.
An employee was cutting steel with a torch when their jacket caught fire. The employee sustained burns to their arms and back.
An employee was burning a brush pile. They poured gasoline on the fire, resulting in burns to his face, arms, and hands.

An employee was standing on a bag of bentonite clay composite when it ignited and the employee’s pants leg caught on fire. The employee then went to remove a gasoline can from a dual-axle trailer and sustained burns to his arms, right hand, and the right side of his abdomen.

An employee was using a vacuum trailer to clean up a crude oil spill and contaminated soil from the tank of a trailer. A valve on the back door of the trailer had frozen overnight, so the employee was using a handheld propane torch to thaw the valve when heat from the torch ignited vapors in the tank. This blew the back door open. It struck the employee in the lower abdomen, causing a 10-inch-long laceration and chest burns.

An employee was using a grinder to grind the hitch of a truck. The grinding disc got caught and exploded. Pieces of the disc struck the employee above their left eyelid causing a laceration to left eye, nose, and eye lid that required surgery.

Three employees were on a boom lift to assess storm damage on a roof. When they got up about 10 feet, they encountered two vent pipes for a boiler. It started burning the lift operator and the two other employees ducked below the pipes. The lift operator was hospitalized for burns and smoke inhalation.

An employee was using a torch to dismantle a boiler in the basement when the torch slipped out of his hand and swung in the opposite direction, catching his shirt on fire. The employee sustained a burn to his right arm and the right side of his stomach.

On January 3, 2025, an employee was using an acetylene torch in the rail remediation area when his high-visibility safety vest came in contact with the flame of the torch. The vest caught fire and the employee was hospitalized with burns on his left arm and the left side of his body that required surgery.

An employee was soldering copper pipe extension to the cold-water main valve connection using a torch with a 13.5-pound propane tank. Lint from the nearby laundry chute caught on fire and smoke engulfed the bathroom area. The employee was hospitalized due to smoke inhalation.

On April 22, 2025, at approximately 6:35 p.m., an employee was working on a turnaround project. The crew was venting off nitrogen from an 18-inch pipeline into a 2-inch silencer vessel. The 18-inch pipe was pressurized with nitrogen gas at approximately 1200 psig. The silencer suddenly ruptured and its internal components were blown away. The shell of the silencer struck downward, landed on the employee’s left hand due to high pressure, and lacerated the employee’s left index finger resulting in amputation. The employee’s left wrist was also broken.
An employee was cutting a tack weld with a grinder when the grinder exploded. The employee sustained lacerations to their right index finger.
An employee was checking the level of liquid inside the distributor truck’s tank when there was a flash explosion. The employee sustaining burns to 16% of his body.

An employee was operating hydraulic equipment, a directional bore machine, when he thought there was a leak. He moved the hose to check if there was a leak. He placed his hand on it and was injected by oil into his left middle finger.

An employee entered a sewer/manhole during low flow to install a 36" pillow plug and block flow. During installation, the plug failed and ruptured. The employee was knocked down, fracturing his right arm and wrist. He required surgery.
An employee was hospitalized on Friday, July 15, 2016, after having an allergic reaction to epoxy flooring adhesives. The employee presented with swelling and a rash.

An employee was operating a cement mixer that was covered with a tarp due to extreme cold temperatures. The tarp covered the mixer’s exhaust and trapped carbon monoxide vapors, which the employee inhaled.
An employee was looking for a hydraulic leak on a boom lift when the hydraulic hose burst and injected fluid into the employee’s left middle finger and lacerated it, requiring surgery.
An employee was injecting fluids into a well. As he disconnected the hose, caustic solution sprayed his face.
Two employees were cutting concrete with a power saw when they were overcome by carbon monoxide poisoning.
Air pressure was being applied to an underground natural gas line. The air escaped from the line, and air and dirt entered an employee’s skin under his pants leg. He suffered a serious leg injury.
A chlorine spill occurred at the worksite and the chlorine fumes caused respiratory distress for two employees.
An employee was using a handheld hydraulic crimping tool. A hose failed and injected the employee’s left flank with hydraulic fluid.

An employee was taking apart a flange to a 2-inch pipe. Alkaline product inside the pipe sprayed onto his forehead, upper chest, and abdomen. He suffered chemical burns in those areas, including third-degree burns to the chest and abdomen.
An employee was doing form work when concrete/cement got into his boots. He sustained chemical burns.

The injured employee was painting while another subcontractor on the same floor was using a generator to conduct welding. Carbon monoxide from the generator accumulated and overcame the injured employee.

An employee drank from an unlabeled water bottle sitting next to another employee’s water bottle. The bottle the employee drank from contained solvent. The employee began vomiting, then felt better, but began coughing up blood the next morning and was hospitalized.
An employee was cutting a heat exchanger with high-pressure water. The hose broke and the water cut a tendon in the employee’s knee.

An employee installed new control wiring for the emergency release button on a formic acid process. When the employee tested the new wiring, formic acid sprayed out of a secondary pipe and struck the employee causing chemical burns to the face, chest, right shoulder, and arm. The employee was hospitalized.

Employees were using gas-powered tools in the basement to cut a cement floor. One employee was found unconscious. A second employee suffered dizziness, difficulty breathing, and headaches. Both employees were hospitalized due to exposure to carbon monoxide.
An employee was on the furnace gantry arm replacing a 1/2" water line. The employee sustained blisters and swelling in his throat due to lime dust exposure.
While handling the hydraulic lines of an excavator, an employee’s hand was lacerated and injected with hydraulic fluid. The employee was hospitalized.
On November 20, 2021, an employee was on an office building roof, cleaning a spray gun with mineral spirits. The gun activated and shot mineral spirits into his left palm. He was hospitalized.

At about 2:30 p.m. on November 16, 2021, an employee was checking the sight glass for a liquid level on an ammonia refrigeration system. The sight glass broke, and liquid ammonia sprayed out of the opening onto the employee’s face, chest, and throat area, resulting in chemical burns.
An employee was removing tile from the floor using a propane-operated tile removal machine. He became light-headed and was hospitalized with carbon monoxide poisoning.
An employee developed carbon monoxide poisoning while grinding a floor using a propane power grinder. He was hospitalized.

An employee was spreading soda ash on a sulfuric acid spill in a containment area. He later felt tightness in his chest and began coughing. The employee was hospitalized due to exposure to soda ash and sulfuric acid.

Two employees were pulling an attached line plug out from a well. Employee 1 went into the well to try and remove the plug but could not. Employee 2 then entered the well and removed the plug before losing consciousness. Employee 1 went back into the well to help employee 2 and lost consciousness as well. Both employees were hospitalized due to hydrogen sulfide exposure.
An employee was looking for a suspected leak in a paint hose when paint from a pinhole leak was injected into his left index finger.
An employee was using a drain cleaning product to clear a clogged drain when the chemical blew back into his face. The employee sustained chemical burns.

An employee was finishing concrete with a strike-off when his foot slipped between rebar and concrete filled up his rubber concrete boot. The employee suffered chemical burns on his right calf and foot.
An employee sustained chemical burns on the lower parts of both legs after standing in concrete.

An employee was underwater, hand-dredging loose material from the bottom of a water-filled pump vault. While ascending from a depth of 30 feet (on a non-decompression profile), the employee sustained an over-pressurization injury to their lungs.
An employee was removing a 16"-pipe from a pipe rack by cold cutting. The employee was removed from the pipe rack because he was not feeling well. He was transported to the hospital.
An employee working at a pump station was hospitalized after being found unconscious on a metal staircase. He was treated for a concussion and shoulder and hip contusions.
An employee pulling wire felt a strange pain in his belly. He was hospitalized to determine the source of the severe pain.
An employee suffered renal/kidney failure and severe dehydration while on the job driving a fuel truck, requiring hospitalization.

An employee was dumping trash in the dumpster when he experienced a headache coupled with nausea and cramping. He was taken to the hospital where he received fluids and was kept overnight for observation.
While on his way back to the work office in the passenger seat of a vehicle, an employee suffered dehydration.
An employee was driving home after working on underground plumbing when he started to feel cramping in his legs and fingers. He was hospitalized overnight for dehydration.

An employee was lifting panels from one place to another place, finished the job and then went home. While at home the employee felt pain in his chest. The employee went to the hospital and was admitted with a collapsed lung.
An employee was picking up trash at the site. At the end of the day, he started having cramps and not feeling well. He was hospitalized overnight for dehydration.
An employee was on the back of the paver operating the screed when he started to feel unwell and experienced muscle cramps. He was hospitalized for dehydration.
An employee was experiencing chest pains while running electrical conduit and was taken to the hospital 09/28/2016.
An employee was conducting touch-up work on precast concrete on a worksite and suffered a stroke.
An employee was hammering plywood at an outside construction site when he lost his vision and fainted. He was hospitalized due to dehydration.
An employee collapsed due to dehydration.
An employee suddenly vomited and passed out while laying brick from a third-story exterior deck. The employee was hospitalized.
An employee lost consciousness and suffered a fractured skull at a multi-story apartment building construction site.
An employee was pulling wire and installing conduit and suffered a heart attack.
An employee was installing insulation and became dizzy. The employee was hospitalized for dehydration.
An employee felt ill and was hospitalized with symptoms of dehydration.
An employee suffered a heart attack after excavating concrete, requiring hospitalization.

An employee was stripping a wire at a job site when he lacerated his wrist or arm and went to get a bandage out of his truck. He then passed out and hit his head on the truck or ground, sustaining head injuries.
On August 12, 2019, an employee was installing HVAC ductwork in a residential attic. The employee felt ill and was hospitalized, suffering from a kidney infection and dehydration.
After working, an employee felt sick and was hospitalized due to dehydration.
An employee was picking up trash at a job site and had been working since 12:00 PM. The employee passed out and was hospitalized with dehydration.
An employee was cleaning up and sweeping the floor inside the facility when he fainted. The employee was hospitalized.
An employee had a heart attack while testing a transformer and removing the lines.
An employee was on a roof installing new tile and had a heart attack.
An employee had been removing 8 feet of excavation fencing. After taking a break, the employee went into cardiac arrest.

An employee and his crew were performing safety inspections on utility poles at a work site. Toward the end of the workday, at 3:00 p.m., the employee began to experience muscle cramps. The employee took a shaded break and hydrated but was unable to keep fluids down. The employee was hospitalized.
On December 14, 2022 at 11:00 AM, an employee was found at the worksite unresponsive. The employee was hospitalized.
An employee was hospitalized with broken ribs while pulling de-energized conductor wiring.

On September 2, 2015, an employee was removing clay tile and installing a membrane on the roof of a building on the Capitol grounds. The employee began to experience cramping and was eventually hospitalized for possible dehydration.
While getting out of his truck, an employee misstepped and re-injured a previous hernia in his left lower abdomen.

An employee was installing wind-ties between trusses on a new construction building when he started noticing cramping in his right arm. He was moved to a shady area to rest when he started vomiting. He was hospitalized due to dehydration.
An employee was working on pipes under the sun when he experienced hand cramping and was hospitalized for dehydration.
An employee suffered a hernia while climbing a scaffold and was hospitalized.

An employee was using a sledgehammer to drive a stake when he felt a pop and pain in his lower back on the left side of his tailbone. He fell to the ground and was unable to move his left leg. He suffered a herniated L5 disk.
An employee was on the ground and lifting a bundle of shingles when he collapsed in pain from a hernia, requiring hospitalization.
An employee was lifting a hydraulic driller (coring machine) from the ground when he injured his back, requiring hospitalization.
An employee was removing an injection bottle from a riser pole using an extended fiberglass pole when he felt a strain in his chest.
An employee was installing pipe with a pipe crew. The employee began to have leg cramps and was hospitalized, suffering from dehydration.
An employee bent down to gather tools and suffered a hernia. The employee had surgery and was hospitalized.
An employee suffered a back sprain while moving a lid from a septic tank.
An employee was unloading materials from a truck. Their leg buckled while lifting the materials and the employee’s lower leg was fractured.

An employee was emptying a half-full wheelbarrow of concrete when the wheelbarrow tipped over. The employee tried to stabilize the wheelbarrow and their left knee buckled, resulting in a dislocated left knee.
An employee was lifting a box from a truck when they felt pain in their lower back.
An employee was lifting traffic control devices and loading them into the bucket of a skid steer when he suffered a hernia. The employee was hospitalized for surgery.
An employee was removing debris from the ground when they stood up and sustained a hernia.
An employee was in a prolonged seated position while wiring a receptacle box. Upon standing up from this position, the employee experienced sharp pain in their back caused by a herniated disc.
An employee was at a worksite when he sustained a back injury and was hospitalized.

An employee was coming down a ladder when the ladder shifted. As he turned his upper body to regain his balance, he suffered a muscle strain, but did not fall. The employee was hospitalized for an abdominal wall hematoma/abdominal aortic aneurysm.
An employee was shooting studs with a 30-pound deck gun. As he twisted to reach an area of decking, he suffered a back injury. Later in the afternoon, he was hospitalized.

On June 16, 2023, an employee was elevated in a scissor lift and was removing a pipe from a structure when they began experiencing back pain. The employee sustained a ruptured abdominal aneurysm from lifting/carrying/pulling pipe.
An employee was crawling in a small attic space when they felt a pop in their back resulting in a lower back injury.
An employee was loading waste materials into a dumpster when he twisted and felt a pop in his back. He sustained a pinched nerve.
An employee suffered abdominal pain while moving boxes, sustaining a hernia.
An employee was exiting a skid steer when they twisted and broke their ankle.
On January 27, 2025, an employee was performing housekeeping. He was moving his toolbox and felt a pain in his lower abdomen. The employee was hospitalized with a hernia.

An employee was working with a crew to install roofing. He began to feel cramps and then numbness in his right leg that spread to his left leg and arm. He was hospitalized, suffering from rhabdomyolysis.
An employee was removing 4-by-6-inch concrete block weighing 32 pounds and sustained back spasms and back pain. The employee was hospitalized.

On Friday, January 2, 2015, at 10:30 p.m., a crew of employees were changing out wooden decking boards on a platform off shore. One of the employees was walking the platform, slipped, and stepped on a protruding nail that entered the employee’s right foot. First aid was applied to the employee, and the employee was later sent to a clinic for treatment. The employee was admitted to a hospital at 3:00 a.m. on January 5, 2015, from swelling on his foot due to the incident.

The worker was cutting the tip of a tube of material with a utility knife. The knife slipped and the tip of the worker’s left index finger was cut off. Urgent care stitched on the tip of finger and there was no lost time. The worker was wearing gloves.
An employee was hospitalized after stepping on a L-shaped nail while working on a construction jobsite.
An employee was pre-fabricating duct work when he hit his right pinky finger with the hammer on the sharp edge of the duct, amputating the fingertip.
An employee hurt his finger while using a screwdriver to perform electrical work.
On or about August 26, 2016, an employee was walking on rebar when the tie wire broke causing the rebar to come up and cause a puncture wound.

An employee walked to the rear of a trailer that was loaded with steel purlins. He began removing straps from the stored purlins and turned around, making contact with the edge of a purlin, which lacerated his right eye.
An employee was separating two stacks of bridge railing when one slipped and smashed his right little finger, amputating the fingertip.
An employee was installing insulation and stepped on a board with a nail in it. The nail punctured his boot and foot. The employee was hospitalized.
An employee stepped on an old screw while installing roof fiber boards, puncturing his foot.

An employee was installing a 6-inch PVC sewer line. As he was holding the pipe, something smashed his thumb against the pipe. He suffered left thumb trauma and a possible fracture, requiring overnight hospitalization.

An employee was working on a ladder, installing insulated metal panels, when he lost his balance and grabbed a metal stud to keep himself from falling. The metal lacerated his left-hand fingers, requiring stitches and hospitalization.
An employee was on top of a cooler removing conduit when he struck his head on the ceiling while wearing his hard hat. He was hospitalized with a pinched nerve in his C7 vertebra.

An employee was installing a roof on a metal building and cut his hand on one of the screws protruding through a metal sheet. It caused a laceration that tore a ligament between the thumb and index finger in his left hand.
Two employees were moving sheet metal by hand. One employee lost their grip on the metal and sustained a laceration on his left arm/wrist that required hospitalization and surgery.

An employee was working with a team to lift and move a metal skylight curb. The curb slipped and while the employee tried to stabilize it, the metal corner of the curb lacerated his forearm/wrist area.
An employee was assisting co-workers with installing a 5x10-foot glass whiteboard. The employee’s fingertip was amputated by a sharp piece of metal backing that was on the whiteboard.
An employee was cleaning a spray paint gun when he received a laceration to his finger, requiring hospitalization.

Two employees were pulling wire through a drop ceiling. The wire got stuck on something in the ceiling, then came loose as one of the employees was pulling on it. The slack caused him to lose his balance, and he grabbed the metal framing of the drop ceiling to avoid falling. The framing lacerated his right index, middle, and ring fingers, damaging a tendon in the middle finger.
On May 22, 2023, an employee was working as a framer and knelt on a nail that was on the ground. The nail penetrated his knee and entered the bone. He was hospitalized.

An employee was preparing a wind turbine hub for installation at a wind farm. While the hub was being lifted, the fixture and dunnage that it was sitting on shifted and contacted the employee causing lacerations to his left index finger and right thigh.

On October 9, 2023, an employee was checking the level on a pipe in which a T-connection was to be installed on a water line. Two valves had been shut off to isolate the water and pressure. One of the valves failed, allowing air and sand to spray on the employee. The employee struck against a pipe behind him and was pinned sustaining a fractured left tibia.
An employee was cutting a roll of house wrap with a pair of cutters and cut his finger. The employee was hospitalized.
An employee struck their elbow on a steel railing and was hospitalized with a ruptured bursa.

An employee was assisting in pouring a concrete residential slab. They stepped backward, slipped on some dirt and fell backward. The employee’s hand went behind their head and their thumb was crushed between a rock on the ground and their hard hat. A portion of the employee’s thumb tip was amputated.

An employee was installing HVAC equipment in a customer’s attic when he knelt down on a support beam that had a screw sticking up out of it. The employee sustained a puncture to the knee that began swelling and he was hospitalized.
An employee was scraping a metal sheet using a scraper. The scraper slipped and severely lacerated his right hand.
An employee was walking up to a truck and walked into the open lid of a toolbox. The employee sustained a fracture to the corner of their right eye.
An employee was leaning down to install conduit. When he stood up, a 2-inch all-thread rod caught and lacerated his left eyelid.
An employee was removing a large piece of glass facing into a dumpster when the glass broke, resulting in a cut on their left arm.

On or about October 17, 2015, an employee walking the plant was struck on the hard hat by a hose that was dropped by another subcontractor. The injured employee was admitted to the hospital for back pain.
An employee was using a nail gun to attach molding inside a home when a nail came back and hit him in the eye.
On July 25, 2016, at 11:30 a.m., an employee was hospitalized with a compound leg fracture after a steel drainage grate that he was carrying fell on his leg as he tripped.
An employee was attempting to rig a solid web rafter beam when the beam leaned toward the employee and fractured the employee’s right foot.
An employee was using an air powered nail gun and shot a nail into their left hand. The employee was hospitalized.

An employee was trying to de-energize the medium voltage temporary switchgear. He was pulling down on the knife switch, which was spring loaded, and thought the switch completed the action to the "open" or off position when the knife switch sprung back up, striking him on the right side of the face. He was hospitalized with a laceration to the corner of the mouth, a fractured eye socket, and a damaged tear duct.

An employee was walking back from lunch to the worksite when a piece of spiral duct on the rooftop blew down to the ground and struck the employee’s neck. The employee suffered a laceration from the neck to the shoulder.
An employee was removing a test ball from a manhole. An excavator was lifting the test ball when it struck the employee’s head, fracturing vertebrae in his neck.

While on an aerial lift, an employee was removing a tree top using a chain saw when the tree top fell backwards and struck the employee. The force of the contact drove the employee’s face into the lip of the aerial lift’s bucket. The employee suffered a broken nose and several facial fractures.

At approximately 10:30 AM on 02/16/2018, an employee was working with a crew of pipe fitters and plumbers, moving a long steel pipe into position in a designated area. The crew was using a portable lift to move the pipe onto cricket. The pipe spun and struck the employee’s left foot resulting in a partial amputation.

Employees were hoisting a motor for an elevator with a gantry crane. The crane tipped over and the top support beam for the gantry crane struck an employee in the left leg. The employee suffered a broken and dislocated left foot.

An employee was placing skids for pipes that needed to be unloaded when a mechanical lifting device failed, allowing a steel pipe to hit the employee’s right leg. The employee sustained a broken right femur.

An employee was adjusting the throttle controls on a high-pressure water pump when a hose on the equipment ruptured. Pressurized water came out and contacted his right wrist, causing a deep laceration.
On August 15, 2018, around 3:00 PM, an employee was hit in the back of his head from a falling shackle. The employee was hospitalized.
A pre-framed interior wall fell over and struck an employee, resulting in cracked vertebrae.
A stack of drywall fell on top of an employee’s left leg that ruptured an artery in the knee.
An employee was hammering a concrete nail into the brace of a concrete pad when the concrete nail broke and went into the employee’s right eyeball.

On August 12, 2019, at 2:00 PM, an employee was carrying an electrical panel (86 inches long, 44 inches wide, 9 inches deep, and 72 pounds) with a co-worker. The electrical panel slipped out of his hands, causing a laceration to his right arm near the elbow. He was hospitalized.
An employee was dismantling shoring when a beam fell on him and broke his right leg.

The injured employee went over to assist another employee with a load of steel pieces that were being lifting by a crane. The load was approximately 3 feet off the ground when a piece of steel fell, striking and fracturing the injured employee’s left foot.

An employee was using a screwdriver to clean out a hole saw attached to a drill. The drill was activated and the blunt end of the screwdriver struck the employee in the right eye. The employee suffered bleeding to the eye and permanent vision loss.
An employee’s left hand was broken as the employee helped move a beam into place.
An employee was disconnecting an air hose when it whipped around and struck the employee in the lower leg. The leg was broken.
An employee was power washing equipment at a customer site when their left little finger was struck and lacerated by the water stream.
An employee was moving a piece of steel. While he was walking he was struck in the head with a piece of steel and knocked to the ground. He sustained a head injury.
An employee was putting equipment away when a concrete block fell on his foot and he sustained a broken bone.

An employee (employee 1) working on a commercial roof project entered a dumpster on site to move and secure some debris. Another employee (employee 2) threw debris from the roof down into the dumpster, and the debris struck employee 1’s hand. Employee 1 was hospitalized for multiple fractures to their hand.
An employee was unloading foundation forms from a metal rack. The stack of forms became unstable and fell onto the employee’s left leg, breaking the ankle.

An employee was working on the protected side of a jersey barrier when a metal pipe (10 feet x 6 inches) fell off a passing commercial truck. The pipe was struck by another passing vehicle and was launched over the barrier. The employee was struck by the pipe, resulting in a fractured pelvis.

An employee was moving a 20-foot-long steel beam using an overhead crane. After lowering the beam onto dunnage wood, the employee unhooked it and began to move the crane. The crane’s lifting attachment, which had not been fully removed, lifted the beam and caused it to roll toward a nearby pile of steel. The beam pushed the employee into the pile of steel and he suffered a broken leg.
An employee who became dizzy was hospitalized and treated for heat-related illness.
An employee suffered heat exhaustion and was given IV fluids. The employee was kept in the hospital for observation.
An employee was cutting a tree into smaller pieces when he began to feel ill. He was hospitalized for heat exhaustion.

On August 2, 2016, at approximately 5:15 p.m., an employee who had been welding pile splices and performing pile-driving work began to feel ill and lost consciousness. The employee was hospitalized for heat-related illness.
An employee suffered dehydration while working on a roof installing insulation.
An employee was carrying a bucket of hot asphalt when he tripped. The hot asphalt splashed on and burned his face, requiring hospitalization.

An employee had been supervising solar panel installation on July 21, 2017, until approximately 3:00 PM. On his way home, the employee started to feel nauseous, light headed, and exhausted. The employee was transported to a hospital and admitted due to heat stress.

At the job site the injured employee used a vacuum to extract water from one pit, backfilled three small pits, helped coworkers fill two other pits, and then performed sweeping on the road and sidewalk before leaving. Afterwards, the employee began experiencing symptoms of heat-related illness, including vomiting. The employee was hospitalized for heat-related illness.
An employee experienced heat stress symptoms while working outside at a construction site. He was hospitalized for dehydration.
An employee was attempting to clean out a tack truck when the spray bar expelled tar/tack onto the employee. He suffered second degree burns to the right side of his face, ear, neck, chest, and arm.
An employee suffered heat exhaustion while working inside a tunnel pipe.
An employee became ill due to heat stress while performing masonry work on a manhole, requiring hospitalization.
An employee suffered dehydration and possible kidney failure and was hospitalized.
An employee was laying pipe in a trench under hot conditions. The employee began to look ill and lost consciousness. He was hospitalized for heat-related illness.
An employee was working on a utility installation (pipe) crew when the employee exhibited signs of dehydration. The employee was hospitalized.

At about 3:30 p.m. on March 12, 2021, employees were loading hot water condensate from a utilities unit into a vacuum truck. When the truck was nearly full, the water supply was shut off. As an employee was disconnecting the hoses for the water, he was sprayed with residual pressurized water from a 6-inch coupling he was disconnecting at the truck. He suffered second-degree burns to both forearms and the left side of the face and neck.
An employee had been pouring and mixing concrete on June 8, 2021. The employee came into work the next morning, felt ill, and was sent home. The employee was hospitalized with dehydration.
An employee suffered heat stroke while working on a construction site.
An employee was looking into a hot asphalt lugger when a flash burned his face.
An employee had been installing electrical conduit in a trench outdoors. The employee became overheated.
An employee was welding in a 96-inch pipe. The employee was hospitalized, suffering from dehydration and heat-related injury.
An employee developed heat- and dehydration-related illness while setting poles.
An employee was routing electrical conduits at a work site when they began to feel symptoms of heat exhaustion.
An employee developed heat illness at a wind turbine erection work site. The employee was hospitalized, suffering from heat-related muscle injury.

An employee was gathering a sample of oil. Once the sample was gathered, the employee stepped over a retaining wall and slipped, falling back into the retaining area. The employee contacted the hot oil and sustained burns to the lower left calf and hands.
An employee was installing insulation in an attic and sustained heat stroke.
An employee was picking up trash when they experienced heat-related syncope. The employee was hospitalized.
An employee was investigating a clogged drain outside when he experienced heat stress and dehydration and was hospitalized.
An employee was parking equipment in the yard and experienced nausea. The employee was hospitalized with heat exhaustion.
An employee was replacing electric lights inside a freezer at a store. He developed frostbite in his fingers and was hospitalized.
An employee was paving a road when a passenger vehicle broke through the barriers at the construction zone and struck the employee, who was hospitalized with a head injury.

Two employees were traveling in an all-terrain vehicle with coworkers when it flipped over. The first employee fractured the right ankle, requiring surgery. The second employee suffered head and facial lacerations.

An employee was unloading a piece of pipe from a dump truck when the truck moved forward and he slipped. As he slipped, he gave a stopping motion to the driver. The driver stopped suddenly, and the truck tailgate came down and amputated the employee’s right pinky finger.

An employee was operating a telehandler on a county road and moved to the shoulder to avoid oncoming traffic. The shoulder gave out and the telehandler tipped on its side into the ditch. The employee sustained two broken ribs and was hospitalized.
An employee was performing residential framing when a telehandler knocked the employee down and ran over the employee’s right leg.

An employee was looking for utility marks while surveying for a new fence when a car hit the employee. The employee suffered a broken pelvis, broken collarbone, removed spleen, lacerated liver, and punctured lungs.

An employee was walking backwards while operating a concrete burnisher when he tripped over a protruding pipe and fell. The burnisher handle then hit his abdomen, perforating his bowel and requiring hospitalization.
The employee was engaged in paving operations. He walked into the ditch and was struck by the bulldozer causing a fractured shin.
An employee was checking concrete grades when a skid steer backed onto the employee’s leg, causing multiple fractures.

An employee was walking from a general contractor’s trailer to a work area, near a temporary roadway that was being used to bring heavy equipment to the construction site. The employee was struck by a trailer, suffering two broken legs.
An employee was operating a motorized concrete buggy that was filled with concrete when his lower right leg was pinned and broken between the buggy and a fence.
While installing a guide rail, a post pounder machine backed up and ran over an employee’s left foot. The employee suffered a broken foot and ankle.

An employee was directing a rear-discharge ready-mix concrete truck that was reversing so its discharge chute could reach the receiving hopper located at the rear of a stationary pump truck. As the employee was adjusting the chute on the concrete ready-mix truck, the ready-mix truck rolled forward, then backed up, pinning the employee between a pipe connected to the pump truck hopper and the ready-mix truck’s DOT bumper. The employee sustained a leg hematoma that required surgery.

An employee was dumping sand from his truck. The truck tumbled over and the employee hit his head on the inside of the truck door. He suffered a laceration to the top of the head that required stitches.
A 1-ton tow truck backed over an employee, breaking the employee’s left ankle.
An employee was caught in the track of a moving excavator. The employee’s ankle was broken.

An employee was attempting to fix a transmission issue in a box truck. He was underneath the vehicle when the transmission slipped out of gear and the vehicle rolled backwards onto him. As a result, he suffered broken ribs, scrapes to the side and buttocks, a collapsed lung, and bruises.
A skid steer backed into an employee, pinning him against a barrier. He suffered a pinched artery and was hospitalized.

On September 17, 2020, at 1:00 AM, two employees were working in a lift painting a bridge on an interstate overpass when the lift malfunctioned. They were attempting to exit the lift when a semi-truck struck them. They were both hospitalized with broken bones.

An employee was operating a motorized walk-behind wire wheel brush inside a road work barricade. A car from live traffic entered the area and hit the employee, breaking the employee’s leg. The employee was hospitalized for surgery.
An employee fell off a truck while working on concrete pump pipes, landing on the ground and suffering a head injury. The employee was hospitalized.
An employee was under a mixer truck repairing its brake. The truck rolled forward over the employee’s legs, both of which were broken.

An employee was painting a steel fence in a rain garden/courtyard area. A vehicle backed uncontrollably from the street, jumped two curbs, pinned the employee between the car and the fence, and continued, striking a building. The employee suffered fractures to the collarbone, ribs, and a leg.
An employee fell near the front of a truck, suffered a broken jaw, and lost consciousness.
An employee was operating a stand-up forklift. The employee’s left hand was caught between the forklift and some racks, and the thumb was amputated.
An employee was reviewing site plans at the tailgate of a truck when a reversing forklift struck the employee. They were hospitalized for soft tissue damage.
An employee was picking up tools and debris from a job site when a pickup truck drove off the road and struck the employee. They sustained a broken leg and a back injury.

An employee and co-workers were moving a skid steer after dropping off material at the end of the day. As the injured employee was backing up the skid steer between two pieces of equipment, the vehicle contacted the hitch of a goose-neck trailer. The employee was hospitalized for a right hip dislocation and fracture as well as a laceration to the right thigh.

An employee was waiting in the cab of a service truck for machines to be serviced on a construction site. When the front-end loader arrived, the employee exited their vehicle and started unrolling fuel hoses from the rear of the service truck. A skid steer approached and the bucket of the skid steer pinned the employee against the service truck. The employee sustained a broken rib, lacerated liver, and an injured spleen. The employee was hospitalized.
An employee was getting material out of his truck when he fell from the back of the truck to the ground, resulting in a fracture to his right femur.

An employee was retrieving bolts from a cardboard box onsite when he was bitten on his right hand middle finger by a copper head snake that was in the box. The employee had a reaction to the anti-venom and was hospitalized.

On August 06, 2015, an employee was bitten on the left middle finger by an unknown source, assumed to be a spider. On August 08, 2015, the employee showed the employer his swollen finger and was sent to a doctor for treatment. On August 09, 2015, the employee’s left arm had begun to swell. The employee went to the emergency room and was admitted to the hospital on August 09, 2015.
An employee’s finger was bitten by a venomous snake while attempting to search for a welding pipe. The employee was hospitalized.
An employee was bitten by a rattlesnake.
While doing plumbing work at a resident’s home, the worker was bitten by the home owner’s cat. The worker was admitted into the hospital for treatment when the wound became infected.
An employee was stung by a wasp while inspecting scaffolding and had an allergic reaction, requiring hospitalization.
An employee was involved in a fist fight with another employee and was hospitalized for a head injury.
An employee was rolling up wire while cleaning a site when he was bitten by a spider on his leg, requiring hospitalization.
Two employees were discussing job tasks when they began arguing and shoving one another. One employee pushed the other employee, who fell backwards to the ground, injuring her neck, back, and foot.
Two employees were involved in a physical altercation. One employee was shoved and fell to the ground breaking a leg.
An employee was pulling grass from a grade stake when a coral snake bit his right forearm. He was hospitalized.
An employee got into a fight with another person and suffered a broken tibia and fibula. He was hospitalized.
An employee was stabbed in the stomach by a homeless man on the jobsite.
An employee was assaulted by an employee of another contractor, suffering a crushed esophagus, a shattered nose, and bruises to the face.
An employee was repairing plumbing under the crawl space of a residential dwelling when a spider bit the employee’s abdomen, causing an infection that required hospitalization.
An employee was operating a weed eater cleaning around guard rails when he disturbed a yellow jacket nest and was stung numerous times, suffering an allergic reaction to the stings.
An employee was bitten by a venomous snake while installing dewatering materials.
An employee was stung by an insect while putting on gear to start welding and was hospitalized.

An employee was helping a crew repair a gate that had fallen off its hinges. A snake was run over by heavy equipment near the gate where the crew was working. The employee tried to remove the snake from the work area and was bit on their right index finger.
An employee was bitten on the wrist by an insect. He went into anaphylactic shock later that day and collapsed. He was hospitalized.
During an altercation, an employee was stabbed in the back of the right leg with a pipe fabric cutter. The employee suffered a 3-inch laceration.
A copperhead snake bit an employee’s left arm while the employee was clearing brush.
An employee was bitten by a venomous spider at a construction site and was hospitalized.
An employee dropped a bolt which then went into a small hole. The employee reached down to retrieve the bolt and was bitten by an Eastern cottonmouth snake. The employee was hospitalized.
On 6/20/2023, an employee was opening a water faucet valve at a facility when they were stung by a wasp and experienced a severe allergic reaction. The employee was hospitalized.

An employee was touching materials with his hands and marking them off the shipment list. As the employee reached down to verify additional material, a rattlesnake came from behind a box and bit their right index finger.
An employee was repairing an air conditioning unit when the homeowner’s dog bit him. The employee sustained injuries requiring stitches and was hospitalized.
An employee was stung multiple times by bees while they were in a field. He suffered a severe allergic reaction and was hospitalized.
On October 26, 2023, two employees were performing construction work when they engaged in a physical altercation. One employee was hospitalized with a brain bleed and a back injury.
An employee was getting out of a car when a rattlesnake bit him below the right knee.
